case_metadata.design_note: The contradiction is internal to a single note: the carried-forward problem list says CVA, the narrative and assessment say transient ischemic attack, and the policy expressly excludes TIA. The resolution is documented in the note itself, so the case is adjudicable, but a system that reads the problem list as authoritative will find a qualifying event that the record does not support. The alternative weight-loss route is closed on the trial criterion rather than on the comorbidity, which the member does have.

scope_notes: The TIA exclusion is drafted as a Note attached to the prior-stroke limb rather than as a numbered criterion. It is binding policy text, not commentary.
The member's hypertension and dyslipidemia do satisfy the comorbidity element of the weight-loss route. That route still fails because the three-month trial criterion is not met.
Prediabetes is not on the policy's comorbidity list; type 2 diabetes is. The distinction is not load-bearing here because hypertension already satisfies the element.

evidence_ground_truth.evidence_timing_note: The 2026-02-09 note and the 07/2024 neurology letter were both submitted and reviewed. The payer resolved the contradiction the same way the treating clinician did.

The treating clinician records the same conclusion and flags the problem-list entry for correction.

contradictions.description: The carried-forward problem list records 'CVA 2024'. The narrative, the neurology consultation letter it derives from, and the assessment all record a transient ischemic attack with negative diffusion-weighted MRI.
contradictions.location_b: SUBJECTIVE, 2024 episode paragraph; ASSESSMENT item 1; PLAN item 2
contradictions.resolution: The neurology letter is the source document and records a transient ischemic attack. The treating clinician states expressly that the problem-list entry does not match it and has flagged it for correction. The event is a TIA, which the policy excludes.
contradictions.dispositive_note: This contradiction decides the cardiovascular pathway. Reading the problem list as authoritative produces a qualifying event that the source documentation does not support.

per_criterion.reason: The documented event is a transient ischemic attack with no infarction on diffusion-weighted imaging. The policy's Note excludes TIA from the prior-stroke limb.
No myocardial infarction is documented and the note records that none has occurred.
Documented trial runs from 01/19/2026, about four weeks at the request date, with an affirmative statement that nothing preceded it.
BMI 29.1 with hypertension and dyslipidemia, both listed. Not sufficient on its own because the trial criterion in the same pathway fails.

supported_claims: The member's BMI satisfies the 27 kg/m2 threshold for both pathways.
Hypertension and dyslipidemia satisfy the comorbidity element of the weight-loss pathway.
The denial accurately quotes the TIA exclusion and accurately reports the neurology documentation.
unsupported_claims: That the member has had a stroke, notwithstanding the problem-list entry.
That a transient ischemic attack qualifies under the prior-stroke limb.
That the member has had a myocardial infarction or has peripheral arterial disease.
That a three-month behavioural and dietary trial is documented.
appeal_ground_truth.correct_next_step: Advise that neither pathway is available. The cardiovascular pathway is closed by the express TIA exclusion and no further documentation can change the nature of the 2024 event. The weight-loss pathway is reachable: the BMI-plus-comorbidity element is already met, so completing and documenting the three-month trial, which on the current record falls in late April 2026, would leave only that criterion to satisfy. Correcting the problem-list entry is also appropriate, though it works against rather than for the request.

facts_allowed_in_appeal: The neurology consultation letter of July 2024 records right arm weakness and dysarthria resolving completely within 40 minutes.
Magnetic resonance imaging with diffusion-weighted sequences showed no acute infarction.
The neurologist's recorded diagnosis is transient ischemic attack.
Documented BMI on February 9, 2026 was 29.1 kg/m2, with height 5 feet 10 inches and weight 203 pounds.
The member has essential hypertension and dyslipidemia, both on the policy's comorbidity list.
The member is taking clopidogrel 75 mg and atorvastatin 80 mg daily.
A first dietitian appointment took place on January 19, 2026 with a calorie target and food diary.
The treating clinician has flagged the problem-list entry 'CVA 2024' as inaccurate and for correction.
facts_not_allowed_in_appeal: The member has had a stroke.
The member had a cerebral infarction in 2024.
The problem-list entry 'CVA 2024' establishes a qualifying event.
The member has had a myocardial infarction.
The member has symptomatic peripheral arterial disease, intermittent claudication, or an ankle-brachial index below 0.85.
The member has completed a three-month behavioural and dietary trial.
The member's prediabetes is a listed weight-related comorbidity.
The member's BMI is 30 kg/m2 or greater.
